note: Refined controlled semantic-subject vocabulary after Research 215 / MC-0019. The catalog defines vocabulary and hierarchy only. It stores no source membership.

membership_policy.assign_when: Assign a subject only when the carrier substantively develops, governs, specifies, evaluates, or preserves durable meaning about that subject.
membership_policy.do_not_assign_when: Do not assign for mere mention, dependency, implementation adjacency, generic cross-cutting relevance, artifact family, authority class, lifecycle, workstream, physical domain, or resolver scope.
membership_policy.secondary_subject_rule: Every secondary subject must independently satisfy the same substantive-content threshold as the preferred subject.
membership_policy.preferred_subject_rule: Choose the best default semantic navigation route for the carrier's primary purpose.
membership_policy.null_preferred_rule: Use null only when two or more assigned subjects are genuinely co-primary and no unique default route is defensible.
membership_policy.preferred_parent_semantics: Display/default hierarchy only. It does not narrow the semantic meaning of the subject.
membership_policy.broader_semantics: Polyhierarchical semantic/navigation relation. Multiple broader parents are allowed.
membership_policy.parent_assignment: Non-assignable parent nodes are never authored as source memberships; parent rollups are derived.
membership_policy.legacy_topics_semantics: Migration/comparison metadata only. Never use legacy_topics as placement guidance.
membership_policy.membership_ownership: Membership remains source-owned or source-adjacent. The vocabulary catalog never enumerates members.

subjects.label: ADS system architecture
subjects.description: Navigation parent for system-level ADS architecture and responsibility boundaries.

subjects.label: Methodological engine
subjects.description: Navigation parent for methodological reasoning, evaluation, retrieval, action and reusable methodological knowledge.

subjects.label: Runtime and tooling
subjects.description: Navigation parent for runtime substrate and developer/tool integration surfaces.

subjects.label: Project development
subjects.description: Navigation parent for the operating method used to develop, preserve and coordinate ADS itself.

subjects.label: Source and evidence
subjects.description: Navigation parent for the Source Universe, source artifacts and evidence substrate.

subjects.label: Project Cockpit
subjects.description: Navigation parent for Project Cockpit product, interaction, visual-language and implementation concerns.

subjects.label: System identity and human/system boundary
subjects.description: What ADS is as a system and how responsibility is divided among the human, LLMs, deterministic software, persistent project state and professional developer workbench.
subjects.include_when: The carrier substantively defines ADS identity, component ownership, autonomy boundaries, human/system responsibility, or the product-level operating boundary.
subjects.exclude_when: The carrier only mentions a model/tool or concerns repository development process without defining the ADS system boundary.

subjects.label: Project state, dependency and orchestration
subjects.description: The product-side project-state model, dependencies, runnable frontier, adaptive sequencing and next-action orchestration.
subjects.include_when: The carrier substantively defines or evaluates project-state semantics, dependency propagation, adaptive orchestration or next-action selection.
subjects.exclude_when: The carrier merely records a development workstream, migration sequence, checkpoint plan or repository task status.

subjects.label: Reusable knowledge representation, activation and lifecycle
subjects.description: How reusable reasoning or methodological knowledge inside ADS is represented, activated, related, versioned, invalidated, consolidated or promoted.
subjects.include_when: The carrier materially develops the representation or lifecycle mechanics of reusable ADS reasoning/methodological knowledge.
subjects.exclude_when: The carrier is primarily about the substantive methodological corpus itself or about preserving project-development knowledge in the repository.

subjects.label: Admissibility, constraints and action authority
subjects.description: Whether an action is permitted, which binding constraints govern it, who has authority to approve or accept residual risk, and when permission/authority requires human gates.
subjects.include_when: The carrier substantively develops action admissibility, constraint provenance, legal/policy/ethical permission boundaries, approval authority, residual-risk acceptance authority or permission-triggered human involvement.
subjects.exclude_when: The carrier is only about evaluation quality, assurance intensity, generic project governance or ordinary review workflow.

subjects.label: Evaluation, falsification, assurance and execution integrity
subjects.description: Scientific/system evaluation, falsification, regression testing, assurance intensity, execution integrity and evidence needed to justify confidence in system behavior.
subjects.include_when: The carrier materially designs, performs or governs evaluation, falsification, assurance controls, regression evidence or execution-integrity checks.
subjects.exclude_when: The carrier is primarily about permission to act or who has authority to approve/accept risk rather than the assurance required once action is admissible.

subjects.label: Runtime, persistence and execution substrate
subjects.description: Durable product runtime state, execution substrate, process/thread/session persistence, resume/recovery semantics and runtime state boundaries.
subjects.include_when: The carrier substantively defines ADS runtime/persistence architecture or durable execution state semantics.
subjects.exclude_when: The carrier is only a local operations runbook, connector setup, developer tool integration or external ecosystem review.

subjects.label: Retrieval, relevance and selective reasoning context
subjects.description: How ADS retrieves, ranks, filters and activates context or methodological knowledge for a concrete project state.
subjects.include_when: The carrier substantively develops retrieval channels, applicability, relevance, methodological horizon, selective context or routing into reasoning.
subjects.exclude_when: The carrier only stores knowledge or describes its general representation without retrieval/applicability semantics.

subjects.label: Recommendation, disposition and action semantics
subjects.description: How ADS represents, ranks, constrains and interprets recommendations, dispositions, action value, blocking/required status and candidate next actions.
subjects.include_when: The carrier materially develops recommendation/disposition/action-value semantics or their evaluation.
subjects.exclude_when: The carrier only describes general project orchestration without recommendation/action semantics.

subjects.label: Methodological Knowledge Universe
subjects.description: The substantive reusable methodological knowledge corpus, its coverage, acquisition, organization and domain content.
subjects.include_when: The carrier materially develops the Methodological Knowledge Universe, its coverage map, source acquisition or substantive methodological content organization.
subjects.exclude_when: The carrier is primarily about the generic representation/lifecycle mechanism used to encode reusable knowledge.

subjects.label: Source Universe and evidence substrate
subjects.description: The Source Universe, Source Vault, source artifacts, ingestion, evidence provenance and durable source/evidence substrate used by ADS.
subjects.include_when: The carrier materially develops Source Universe architecture, source-vault operation, ingestion, artifact integrity or source/evidence provenance.
subjects.exclude_when: The carrier only uses sources as ordinary evidence for another subject.

subjects.label: Development governance, continuity and repository method
subjects.description: The operating method for developing ADS: repository integrity, continuity, branching, commits, checkpoints, routing, review and preservation discipline.
subjects.include_when: The carrier substantively governs or evaluates the project-development method, repository process, continuity, commit/checkpoint discipline or development routing.
subjects.exclude_when: The carrier is about the architecture of project knowledge itself rather than how development work is operated.

subjects.label: Project-knowledge architecture and reconstruction
subjects.description: Architecture for ownership, preservation, identity, reconstruction, migration and navigation of project-development knowledge.
subjects.include_when: The carrier materially designs or evaluates how durable project knowledge is owned, identified, migrated, reconstructed or navigated.
subjects.exclude_when: The carrier only specifies day-to-day repository process or concerns reusable product-side methodological knowledge.

subjects.label: Multi-model collaboration and review protocol
subjects.description: Collaboration protocols among ChatGPT, Claude, Codex, Claude Code and future model collaborators, including task ownership, independent review and evidence handoff.
subjects.include_when: The carrier materially defines or evaluates multi-model collaboration, review modes, write ownership, model handoffs or interaction-session coordination.
subjects.exclude_when: The carrier merely mentions that another model was used.

subjects.label: Developer tooling, local execution and external integrations
subjects.description: Developer tools and integration surfaces used to build, operate or connect ADS, including local execution bridges, MCP/connectors, external APIs and development-runtime tooling.
subjects.include_when: The carrier materially develops, evaluates or operates a developer/tool integration or external connection used by ADS development or operation.
subjects.exclude_when: The carrier primarily defines ADS product runtime/persistence state rather than a tool/integration surface.

subjects.label: Project Cockpit product architecture
subjects.description: Overall Project Cockpit product/world/control architecture and the product-level composition of its major surfaces.
subjects.include_when: The carrier materially develops the Cockpit as a whole product or its broad world/control architecture.
subjects.exclude_when: The carrier is narrowly about interaction behavior, visual grammar or implementation provenance without broader product architecture.

subjects.label: Cockpit interaction, focus and conversation workspace
subjects.description: Cockpit interaction mechanics such as focus, selection, zoom, context suppression, conversation workspace behavior and user-control interactions.
subjects.include_when: The carrier materially designs or validates Cockpit interaction/focus/workspace behavior.
subjects.exclude_when: The carrier is only about static visual styling or implementation provenance.

subjects.label: Cockpit WorkUnit, connector and visual grammar
subjects.description: Cockpit semantic visual language, including WorkUnit silhouettes/categories, connectors/ports, relation appearance, visual hierarchy and related grammar.
subjects.include_when: The carrier materially designs or validates the semantic visual grammar of Cockpit objects or relations.
subjects.exclude_when: The carrier only concerns interaction behavior or implementation source binding.

subjects.label: Cockpit implementation fidelity and provenance
subjects.description: Implementation fidelity, source binding, provenance recovery, accepted implementation manifests and exact-history/implementation integrity for Project Cockpit.
subjects.include_when: The carrier materially governs or verifies Cockpit implementation fidelity, accepted source mapping, provenance or recovery.
subjects.exclude_when: The carrier is only conceptual product/interaction/visual design without implementation-fidelity concerns.
